nodes.title: READ ME FIRST!
widgets_values:
This WAN2.2 workflow can do i2v with two- or three-KSamplers and has optional GGUF checkpoint loading. You can then chain together up to 4 clips, using the last frame of the previous clip each time to generate a longer video.

To use GGUF checkpoints, ensure that the red "Use GGUF Models?" is set to "true" and ensure you have loaded the GGUF model and GGUF CLIP in the "Models Loader" group. To use regular .safetensors checkpoints, set this to "false".

You can either run with 2 KSamplers (x + x steps) or 3 KSamplers (x + x + x steps). If you want to run in 2-sampler mode, ensure the red "Use 2 Samplers?" node is set to "true" AND you have disabled the "Step 2" group in the Fast Group Bypasser node.
NB. Make sure that your "Total Steps" node has a number that is exactly divisible by 2 or 3, depending on the number of KSamplers you want to use.

Download the models in the note below and ensure they are in the correct folders.

Choose a latent Video resolution, some examples I use are:

480 x 480
480 x 688
480 x 640
480 x 720

Optimal length (Latent Video Node) is 81 for WAN, but up to 121 can work.

The workflow will save each clip as an individual file as well as concatenating them into longer clips sequentially. It will also save a .png of the "last frame" from each clip, which shows you what was used as the first frame for the next one. You will need to enter appropriate folder/filenames for all the image and video save nodes.

Insert your starting image and fill out the prompts as you wish.

For Loras - If using lightning loras, Step 1 has no lightning lora, Step 2 and Step 3 use the high noise and low noise lightning loras respectively. Add any other loras you want, but it's a good idea to add them to all two/three steps.

For the upscaling you can choose a model and then downscaler. I use remacri 4x then downscale again. With the default settings, a 480p generation will upscale to 720p using this method. Upscaling can take a long time on longer videos, so I prefer to test without it and then enable it if I like the generated video.

For the interpolation, it is a rule of thumb to use a multiplier of 3 or 4 with a length of 81 to get a decent speed on a 60 FPS final video. The final video frame rate and multiplier work together to give you the final speed/length of video so you might need to experiment based on your prompts and loras! 

The workflow will automatically rescale your input image to match the dimensions of the generation latent video. This can help with artifacting if you are using a much larger image as an input.

Lastly, as a point of use - the best way I have found of using this workflow is to disable clips 2, 3, and 4 and generate the first clip, ensuring the Seed is "fixed". Then if I am happy with clip 1, I enable clip 2 and generate that one, then continue in this manner. As long as you don't change any of the settings for the earlier clips, the workflow won't regenerate them. If you try to generate all 4 at once and then find out clip 1 was rubbish, you'll waste a lot of time! 

NB. Each clip has a different seed set. This is by design, as SVI works best with a different seed for each clip. I often set them to be different and then fix them while I work out the best prompts/loras/etc.

NB. Enabling a clip will automatically enable the "step 2" group for that clip, as well as the upscaling. You must remember to turn these off if you are not using them!

There are shortcut nodes to travel aroudn the workflow. Pressing 1 will take you to the initial inputs and settings. Pressing 2, 3, 4, 5 will take you to clips 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively.

Note: The workflow will interpolate twice for each clip if you enable upscaling. This is not a bug - if we don't run two interpolate nodes then the only option is to upscale AFTER interpolation and this can take a *very* long time.
